narrative.overview:
sqwer is set like a printed piano method. Typing is taught as notation: every typed letter sits on a five-line staff in Geist Mono, its finger number (1 thumb to 5 little finger, counted per hand) engraved above it in that finger's colour, and the course is one score of twelve measures read left to right under an ultramarine playhead. Staves, numerals, bar lines and tempo terms are working grammar that carries real information (which finger, which chapter, what speed); they are never ornament, and the page does not dress as a concert hall.

The paper is cool porcelain, the ink is near-black navy, and one ultramarine does exactly two jobs: the action and the playhead. Five finger colours are the only other chromatic voice, and they always travel with a numeral. PP Altera Serif sets titles like engraved score headings; PP Neue Montreal carries prose; Geist Mono carries anything typed or measured. Density is generous and calm: wide sections, long measures, hairlines instead of boxes, so that the typing surface is the loudest thing on any screen. Night mode is deep navy, not grey, and keeps the same grammar.

Motion is a playhead. Things sweep left to right, ease out from visible defaults, and stop. On the landing page the whole page is that score: scrolling down slides the panels sideways under a fixed playhead. Around a typing surface everything else recedes; under reduced motion every loop, scrub and entrance is removed and the content stands complete.
keyCharacteristics: Every typed glyph is set on a staff with its finger numeral above it, in its finger colour.
One ultramarine for the action and the playhead; nothing else is ultramarine-filled.
Serif titles at weight 400, serif numerals at 800, mono for typed text and figures, sans for prose.
Hairlines and tonal bands, never cards or shadows, structure the page.
Every corner is 3px; noteheads and numeral discs are the only true curves.
A playhead sweeps left to right; nothing else moves for long.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Ultramarine fills the action and draws the playhead. It never fills a decorative surface, a heading or a second competing button.

rules.name: The Numeral Escort Rule
rules.body: A finger colour never appears without its numeral or a label beside it. Colour is not the only signal.

rules.name: The Chord Rule
rules.body: The only background gradient is the chord: a faint (16% opacity) horizontal wash of the five finger colours, mirrored about the thumbs (little, ring, middle, index, thumb, index, middle, ring, little), masked to fade at top and bottom. It sits behind a staff, nowhere else (not behind the closing panel, which stands on the plain page). The 56px fade at the right edge of the pinned score is a veil of the page colour that makes the next measure arrive rather than be cut; it carries no hue and is not a second gradient. A single finger's wash fading from fingertip to palm inside the hands engraving is colouring, not a second gradient.

rules.name: The Typewriter Rule
rules.body: Anything the learner types, and any number that is counted, is set in Geist Mono. Prose is never mono.

rules.name: The Engraved Numeral Rule
rules.body: Finger numbers and chapter numbers are Altera Serif at weight 800; headings stay at 400. Weight belongs to numerals, not titles.

rules.name: The Engraved Page Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with lines, not lifted with shadows. If a surface needs separation, give it a tonal band or a hairline.

dos: Do set every typed glyph in Geist Mono on a five-line staff, with its finger numeral (piano convention per hand, thumb 1 to little finger 5) above it in that finger's colour.
Do keep Ultramarine (#3355FF) to the action, the playhead and the next-key cue; render every other emphasis in Engraving Ink weight.
Do use 3px for every rectangular corner, and reserve curves for noteheads and numeral discs.
Do separate sections with hairlines and full-bleed Porcelain Band, not shadows or boxed cards.
Do move things as a playhead moves: left to right, ease out (out-expo), from visible defaults, then rest; loops play three times and stop.
Do put every animation under the reduced-motion media condition so it disappears in one place.
Do give a pinned score a way to know where you are (a playhead label and a timeline) and a way to jump (the timeline links), and keep the next measure partly visible at the right edge.
Do limit entrance to the rise, and only for what arrives from the right; leave what is on screen at load still.
Do give every figure a unit and a definition in a caption beneath its scale.
Do write copy in formal British English, sentence case, with no contractions, exclamation marks or em dashes.
donts: Don't place small labels above headings. In this world labels belong to a mark: a bracket, the playhead, a scale tick.
Don't use a finger colour without its numeral or a text label.
Don't add a second background gradient; the chord behind a staff is the only one.
Don't use staves, numerals or tempo terms as ornament: each must carry a real finger, chapter or speed.
Don't dress the page as a concert hall: no instruments or sheet-music textures.
Don't add a second filled button beside Get started.
Don't use drop shadows to lift surfaces.
Don't rely on the horizontal score below 900px, under reduced motion or in short windows; the vertical page must carry the same content in the same order.
Don't animate numbers up to their value in headlines.
